slot.brief: Given atomic masses of a nucleus X(A,Z) and X(A−1,Z) plus a neutron, compute the neutron separation energy from the mass defect — careful with electron masses when using atomic masses.

stem: The atomic masses of $^{49}_{26}\text{X}$ and $^{48}_{26}\text{X}$ are $48.954918$ u and $47.952253$ u, respectively. Given $m_n=1.008665$ u and $1\ \text{u}c^2=931.5$ MeV, find the neutron separation energy. Take $m_e=0.000549$ u.

verdicts.working: Neutron separation energy: \(S_n=[M(^{48}X)+m_n-M(^{49}X)]c^2=(0.006000\,\mathrm u)(931.5\,\mathrm{MeV/u})=5.589\,\mathrm{MeV}\). Atomic-electron masses cancel.

working:
$S_n=[M(^{48}_{26}\text{X})+m_n-M(^{49}_{26}\text{X})]c^2$; the equal electron counts in the atomic masses cancel. $S_n=[47.952253+1.008665-48.954918](931.5)=5.589\ \text{MeV}$.

Independent check: Neutron separation energy: \(S_n=[M(^{48}X)+m_n-M(^{49}X)]c^2=(0.006000\,\mathrm u)(931.5\,\mathrm{MeV/u})=5.589\,\mathrm{MeV}\). Atomic-electron masses cancel.
solution:
The neutron separation energy is $S_n=[M(^{48}_{26}\text{X})+m_n-M(^{49}_{26}\text{X})]c^2$; the equal electron masses in the atomic masses cancel.
$$S_n=[47.952253+1.008665-48.954918](931.5)=5.589\ \text{MeV}$$
